item.title: “Tere Bin” star Wahaj Ali in Dhaka with Nusraat Faria
item.description:
Pakistani actor Wahaj Ali rose to fame for playing Murtasim in the popular drama series Tere Bin. Beyond Pakistan, he has gained a strong following among audiences in Bangladesh, India and across South Asia.

The actor recently appeared at a fashion show in Dhaka. On Saturday evening, Wahaj Ali attended an event titled “Emira: The Wedding Chapter” at the United Convention Centre in Dhaka.

Actress Nusraat Faria also attended the fashion show. During a break from the show, Faria posted a photo with Wahaj on Facebook.

In the caption, she wrote, “I walked proudly in Jamdani, represented with love, and created memories.” The photo of the two stars quickly spread across social media.

In the photo, Nusraat Faria wore a dark purple strapless lehenga-choli featuring Jamdani motifs. She accessorised the outfit with a tikli, a heavy necklace, jhumkas and golden bangles. Wahaj, meanwhile, wore a dark blue formal suit with a matching shirt.

The photo received more than 5,500 reactions, while many users also left comments. A Facebook user named Nurul Amin wrote, “Now you should make a film with Wahaj.”

Miss World Bangladesh 2026 winner Samanzar Sayeed and several others also took part in the fashion show.

Wahaj Ali is a familiar face in Pakistani television dramas. He made his acting debut in 2015 with the drama Ishq Ibadat. He subsequently appeared in several series, including Ishq Jalebi, Dil Naawaz and Fitoor.

However, Tere Bin brought him international recognition. The drama, which began airing in 2022, featured Wahaj as Murtasim Khan opposite Yumna Zaidi. The story and the chemistry between the two actors received an overwhelming response from audiences.

Sheikh Hasina’s activities in India main challenge to PM’s Delhi visit
item.description:
The “principal challenge” in planning Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to India is the activities of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and leaders of her party currently staying there, Foreign Affairs State Minister Humaiun Kobir has said.

He made the remarks in an interview with Indian newspaper The Hindu on Monday.

Responding to questions from The Hindu on the sidelines of the Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026, organised by the Centre for Governance Studies (CGS) in Dhaka, Humaiun Kobir said India needed to realise “the challenges facing the newly elected government” in Bangladesh.

He also said the activities of leaders of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned in the country, while in exile would not be helpful to India.

‘Destabilising another country’

Urging India to restrain Sheikh Hasina and her exiled party leaders, Humaiun Kobir said in the interview that the visit will be bilateral, but there are some challenges, and both sides will overcome them through dialogue.

According to him, Bangladesh was not asking for too much when it comes to the main challenge. “Sheikh Hasina and her team are staying in Delhi and they are trying to destabilise another country from there. This is not helping India either.”

Humaiun Kobir accused Sheikh Hasina of being responsible for the deaths of nearly 2,000 Bangladeshi citizens during the suppression of the July-August 2024 uprising. He described her as “a terrorist”.

He said Bangladeshis needed a “clean break” with their past, as people had sacrificed their lives in the process of ousting Sheikh Hasina’s government, which had remained in power for more than 15 years.

The state minister, however, said that discussions with India were under way and that Dhaka welcomed the dialogue.

Describing relations with India as a priority for Dhaka, Humaiun Kobir told The Hindu, “We are seeing some positive signs as India is trying to restrain them. That is the norm between two countries. If they (Hasina and her team) are restrained, then there will be no problem in the [bilateral] relationship.”

Highlighting the role of Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi in this regard, Humaiun Kobir said, “The visit of the Prime Minister will take place at a conducive time and I am hopeful. The PM has never said that he will not visit [India].”

Indian high commissioner’s role

Describing the Awami League leadership as an “obstacle” to normalising Dhaka-Delhi relations, Humaiun Kobir said, “The Indian High Commissioner here is doing a good role. He is trying and hopefully Delhi will be receptive to his opinion and if they give importance to his opinion, then we are ready to engage across the board. We are carrying out our consultations.”

The state minister said Bangladesh was ready to discuss all issues but expected some “reciprocation”.

Saying that Bangladesh would not allow anyone to operate from Dhaka against India’s interests, Humaiun Kobir said he expected India to take similar measures.

“When two governments sit down to discuss keeping in mind national interests, all issues can be addressed,” he told The Hindu.

The Hindu correspondent is visiting Dhaka as a guest of the Centre for Governance Studies to attend the Bay of Bengal Conversation 2026.

item.title: Applications open for news presenters at BTV for both Bengali and English
item.description:
A great opportunity has emerged to present news on Bangladesh Television (BTV), one of the country’s oldest, most established and prestigious media institutions.

For those who have long dreamed of building a career in television through fluent delivery, clear pronunciation and confident presentation, this is an excellent opportunity.

Bangladesh Television has invited applications from interested and eligible candidates to present news in both Bengali and English.

Joining the state-owned broadcaster as a news presenter is not only a professional achievement but also a position of considerable responsibility and prestige, involving the delivery of reliable information to millions of people across the country.

How to apply

The authorities have set specific rules and guidelines for candidates wishing to take part in the audition and selection process.

Applicants must prepare a complete curriculum vitae (CV) with a photograph, including a recent passport-size or other required photograph.

The CV should clearly state the applicant’s educational qualifications, experience in language and pronunciation skills, and contact details.

Applicants must submit their applications by 7 October 2026. As only a few days remain before the deadline, interested candidates are advised to prepare their applications promptly and send them to the designated address.

How to submit your application

Candidates can submit their applications through several convenient channels, allowing applicants from across the country to apply easily. Those wishing to apply in person or by post can send their applications by courier or post to the designated address:

Deputy Director-General (News), Bangladesh Television, Headquarters Building, Rampura, Dhaka-1219.

In line with modern digital communication, applicants can also submit their applications electronically. They can send their CV with a photograph and application through the official email address (newsaudition@btv.gov.bd) or via WhatsApp at 01332125138.

Bangladesh Television’s news presenter selection process is highly competitive and transparent.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for those with strong language and pronunciation skills, an individual style of news presentation, and the ability to present contemporary issues fluently.

For young and experienced media professionals who aspire to appear on BTV and begin a new chapter in their media careers through news presentation, this opportunity is highly significant.

Submit your application with a complete CV to the designated address or through the digital channels and take the opportunity to work with Bangladesh Television.

item.title: ‘I paid for my uniform with bribes to take bribes’
item.description:
A video circulating on social media shows Mohammad Elias Hossain, an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) of Chunarughat Police Station in Habiganj, saying, “I paid for my uniform with bribes so that I could take bribes.”

Elias Hossain reportedly made the remarks while visiting Ranigaon Bazar in Chunarughat upazila as part of an investigation into a case. A local resident recorded his remarks on a mobile phone. The video later spread on social media, drawing criticism.

In the video, ASI Elias Hossain is heard saying, “People say things only after seeing something happen, don’t they? Don’t you understand? If I say I’m a police officer and I don’t take bribes, I am the imam of Baitul Mukarram would it be believable? I paid for my uniform with bribes, so that I could take bribes.”

According to local sources, ASI Elias Hossain had gone to Ranigaon Bazar to investigate a case filed by Noman Mia, a businessman there. He made the remarks in front of people who were present at the time.

Meanwhile, several local residents have alleged that ASI Elias Hossain has demanded bribes while investigating various cases. They claimed that he shows little interest in investigating cases unless he is paid a bribe.

Allegations of irregularities had also emerged against Elias Hossain while he was investigating a case filed over allegations of child abuse and attempted rape in Tekarghat village of Gazipur Union in the upazila. The allegation is that he took financial benefits from the defendants and pressured and intimidated the complainant to withdraw the case.

Local residents have also alleged that Elias Hossain exercises influence at the police station and in investigations by identifying Officer-in-Charge (OC) Saiful Islam of Chunarughat Police Station as his “big brother” in the area. However, the allegation could not be independently verified.

When contacted about the video, ASI Mohammad Elias Hossain said, “I don’t know anything about this.” He then disconnected the phone.

When contacted by phone, Chunarughat Police Station OC Saiful Islam said, “I have seen the video. It is being verified. I will sit down with him [ASI Elias Hossain] to try to find out the context in which he made the remarks.”

PM joins Children’s Rights Day, Shishu Academy’s 50th anniversary event
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday joined a program marking Children’s Rights Day 2026 and the 50th anniversary of Bangladesh Shishu Academy.
The three-day observance is being held at Bangladesh Shishu Academy in the capital from October 6 to 8, with this year’s theme “Let every child have a secure future.”
Around 150 children welcomed the prime minister upon his arrival at the venue in the morning.
The event began with the national anthem, after which the prime minister took his seat alongside other guests.
Prime minister’s wife and Ziaur Rahman Foundation Vice-Chairman Dr Zubaida Rahman were present at the program, chaired by Women and Children Affairs Minister Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain.
The program features a cultural performance by children, presentation of commemorative gifts to children and the unveiling of the souvenir titled Shaishab.
The prime minister is also scheduled to interact with children from different parts of the country through a videoconference.
He will also visit an exhibition featuring paintings by children and a photo gallery.
After the program, the prime minister will visit the Children’s Museum building and inaugurate a solar panel system and a substation on its ground floor.

item.title: Dengue cases surge in Chittagong, 21 deaths recorded this year
item.description:
The dengue outbreak in Chittagong is intensifying, with 4,914 infections and 21 deaths recorded in the district between January 1 and October 5.
The situation worsened sharply in September, when 2,430 cases and 16 deaths were reported.
According to the District Civil Surgeon’s Office, 107 new dengue cases were detected in the 24 hours until 8am on Sunday. Of the 4,914 patients recorded this year, 260 are currently undergoing treatment at different hospitals, while 4,654 have recovered and been discharged.
The dengue situation remained relatively mild at the beginning of the year, with 68 cases in January, 22 in February, 20 in March, 29 in April and 37 in May.
Cases began rising in June, reaching 122 that month, followed by 536 in July and 1,202 in August. The number surged to 2,430 in September.
Another 448 cases were reported in the first five days of October.
September was also the deadliest month, accounting for 16 of the 21 deaths recorded this year. Two deaths each were reported in July and August, while one was recorded in February.
No new dengue deaths were reported in the 24 hours preceding the latest update.
According to data from the District Civil Surgeon’s Office, 2,285 of the 4,914 cases were reported in Chittagong city, 2,098 in different upazilas and 531 among patients who came from other districts.
Among the upazilas, Sitakunda recorded the highest number of cases at 620, followed by Karnaphuli with 285, Banshkhali 154, Rangunia 152, Satkania 121, Anwara 112, Raozan 103 and Patiya 100.
Other cases were reported in Hathazari (84), Chandanaish (77), Boalkhali (76), Mirsharai (79), Lohagara (66), Fatikchhari (44) and Sandwip (25).
Of the total dengue patients recorded this year, 2,402 are men, 1,403 are women and 1,109 are children.
Among the 107 patients admitted in the 24-hour period, 56 were men, 23 were women and 28 were children.
However, women accounted for the highest number of deaths. Of the 21 people who died, 11 were women, six were children and four were men.
The number of dengue cases recorded in Chittagong this year has already surpassed the totals for the previous two years.
The district recorded 4,323 cases and 45 deaths in 2024, while 4,864 cases and 27 deaths were reported in 2025.
As of October 5 this year, the number of cases stood at 4,914, with 21 deaths.
Residents have complained that mosquito-control activities in Chittagong have not kept pace with the rising number of dengue cases.
Muntasir Uddin, a resident of Sangeet Residential Area in Hamzarbag, said mosquito infestations in the area had become severe, while City Corporation workers assigned to mosquito control were rarely seen.
He also alleged a lack of supervision over the effectiveness of insecticide spraying.
Jamal Uddin, a resident of Chandanpura, said the number of dengue patients in the city had increased significantly, but City Corporation monitoring had not increased proportionately.
District Civil Surgeon Mohammad Sajedur Rahman told Bangla Tribune that dengue is a mosquito-borne disease and urged residents to keep their surroundings clean.
He said dengue could be controlled by destroying mosquito breeding grounds and advised people to undergo dengue tests and seek medical advice promptly if they develop a fever.
Sheikh Fazle Rabbi, divisional director of health in Chittagong, also advised people to consult a doctor immediately if they develop fever or symptoms of dengue.
He said the most important measure to prevent dengue was to destroy Aedes mosquito breeding grounds, while efforts should also be made to eliminate adult mosquitoes.
He said the City Corporation had been sent several letters urging it to intensify mosquito-control activities.
Ashraful Amin, chief executive officer and secretary of Chittagong City Corporation, told Bangla Tribune that the corporation was conducting regular mosquito-control activities to combat dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases.
He said special “crash programmes” were also being conducted in different areas when necessary.
Amin said dengue could not be controlled through insecticide spraying alone and stressed the need to destroy mosquito breeding grounds.
He also urged residents to prevent water from stagnating in and around their homes, rooftops, construction sites and other areas.

item.title: Dhaka ranks first globally in air pollution
item.description:
Dhaka ranked first among the world's most polluted cities on Tuesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 213 at 11:10am.
The air quality was classified as "very unhealthy", signalling a serious health alert where everyone may experience health effects, according to the AQI scale.
Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia ranked second with an AQI score of 208, while Singapore in Singapore ranked third with a score of 179 and Kolkata in India ranked fourth with an AQI score of 177.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Hair is political
item.description:
When I was six, I contracted a severe case of typhoid. I had to get injections for ten days straight.
My relatives recommended that I shave my hair off. I would be willing to shave my hair for the right cause today without hesitation, just like my favorite fashion designer, Vivienne Westwood.
She shaved her hair to raise awareness for climate change. But this was too terrifying for my six-year-old self. I had grown my hair out for a while, and I was afraid to let it all go.
Furthermore, I was too sick to even understand what was going on with me. I only remember sitting on the balcony under the sun with my Naan while she carefully brushed my hair and ran a razor over my head.
That was the first time I remembered how my face looked without hair. I was quickly taught the realities of society that hair is everything, especially if you are a woman.
One of my favorite scenes from Fleabag is when her sister gets a bad haircut in a moment of weakness, and she reframes it by saying, “Claire, it's French," because the worst thing you can do as a woman is not look palatable and resist the patriarchal male gaze.
To become the worst thing this society has encountered is to be an angry feminist who doesn’t shave her body hair or cuts her hair too short.
Hair is political, be it for Black women who had to fight to be taken seriously in their Afro hair or Chinese women who dye their hair pink right before graduation to honor Zheng Linghua, who committed suicide because she was cyberbullied for her hair color.
In a world where Iranian woman Mahsa Amini is beaten to death because her hair was not properly covered, it is equally political if you are a South Asian or Bengali woman raised in a conservative Muslim household.
I grew up in a small, secluded area in Puran Dhaka called Hazaribagh. Boys played cricket and rode bicycles, filling my neighborhood. Meanwhile, little girls enjoyed playing Kanamachhi and Ekka-Dokka.
I was a restless, clumsy, boyish child whom the boys made fun of because I wanted to play with them.
When I was about four years old, I stole my brother’s shirt, wore it, and ran away from my house. I assumed I was indistinguishable from boys my age which could not be further from the truth.
I was a rebellious child with a bowl cut who wanted to play cricket with boys and ruin my clothes with dust.
People around me didn’t quite like it. My parents were desperate to find a school that was as diligent about grades and cultural activities as it was strict about instilling manners.
They found the school they wanted. With its merits, this school also instilled in me a fear of judgment.
My mother used to make two ponytails when I had short hair; it was the dress code. I never questioned it. I did not have long hair until I was in third grade.
When my hair grew longer, different rules started to apply to me. Now, it was mandatory for me to make two braids. I still did not question it.
Every morning, my mother would braid my hair. Meanwhile, my father ironed his shirt, humming "Amar Sara Deho Kheo Mati" by Andrew Kishore.
As I never questioned the decision of making two mandatory pigtails, I never suffered the consequence of breaking the dress code.
Until my mother received a diagnosis of a chronic illness at the end of my fourth grade, I had nobody to braid my hair.
I brushed my hair in a disheveled manner and made one big ponytail. My father dropped me at school. For the first time, I was about to break the rule.
So long, I had only seen what happened to the girls who didn’t brush their hair according to the rules.
Sometimes, if you were lucky, you were only yelled at.
If your class teacher was strict, you got threats of having your hair chopped off.
If your luck was terrible, you might get slut-shamed for your hairstyle. This would happen even if you were in grade four.
Accusing you of luring men at an all-girls school is both unfair and ridiculous. You only wanted to style your hair differently.
After fifth grade, I switched to a different school. It was a combined school where boys would study in the day shift and girls in the morning. I was hoping things would be different here.
To my disappointment, your hair still dictated your reputation. Breaking the rule of two mandatory pigtails was equivalent to wearing the Scarlet Letter.
We were taught to treat people like they were aliens or as if they were a different species just on the basis of our assigned genders at birth. Segregated schools made it worse.
It’s as if we are peeking at the zoo animals when one shift ends and another one starts.
It didn’t help that most of our teachers were head-to-toe misogynistic; some of them were women. Male teachers and female teachers showcased different cases of misogyny. Male teachers displayed either benevolent misogyny or inappropriate behavior.
Benevolent misogyny meant they believed women needed protection, so they wouldn’t hit female students but felt free to abuse boys.
Inappropriate behavior included flirting that bordered on harassment and even attempted grooming.
From female teachers, the accusations felt more guttural and personal. It typically began with thinly veiled concerns and concluded with slutshaming.
Despite society's constant pressure on girls to meet beauty standards, they still face shame for their hairstyles and their desire to look ornate.
There was a strong association in the minds of these women that these school girls only wanted to doll up, wear their ponytails instead of two braids, and plump their lips with fruity chapsticks to entice the boys from the day shift.
They would try to warn us by telling us that we should be independent instead of chasing a man, but their heteronormative assumptions that only a boy can be the object of desire in a girl’s world, suggesting that this is the sole focus for teenage girls, reinforce harmful stereotypes and promote heteronormative behavior.
This type of social indoctrination is what keeps so many women in shackles of compulsory heterosexuality.
Today, I am in university, and I have the freedom to cut, dye, and wear my hair however I want.
To this day, I still cannot find the answer to a question.
How is your hair a testament to your character?
Asmita Mehefin likes to look at the moon and write poems and compare how the celestial bodies are similar to the web of life inside our own bodies.

item.title: The Strange Grief of Turning 18
item.description:
To me this birthday was not special because I turned 18; sadly, the breeze of responsibility and the fear of adulthood have not crept into my life yet. However, the reason this birthday lingered within me for quite long is because this was that day when I actually felt the time flying.
If I am to leave for my universities abroad next year, this would be my last September in Dhaka.
Last September, October, and all the last. In fact, maybe the last birthday that I ever get to celebrate in my own home with my own people.
For the last two or three years, I had this tradition I followed. I bought cake from my favorite bakery and cut the cake the night before my birthday.
There was always something about waking up the morning of your birthday and having the leftover cake from midnight.
This time though, I could not really stick to that.
I returned from my coaching classes, and my sister came home from her university classes a lot later and jumped straight to her online meetings. Maybe I was physically drained out from fatigue or just mentally drained out; I could not even stay awake till 12.
My body was giving up, and I did not want it to get consumed with all the birthday depression, reflections, and everything. But well, I think I failed at that; here we are talking about life again.
I woke up in the morning, put on the dress I had chosen in my mind, and got a birthday photoshoot done, this time with flowers.
I never bought flower bouquets on my birthday, but for this last time I thought I would.
On my way back from tuition in Dhanmondi, right beside the bakery was that flower shop I always wanted to buy flowers from.
And the occasion could not have been more perfect.
Something so memorable about this birthday would be that on my way back with the flowers and cake, when I was on a rickshaw ride home, I saw a star.
Yes, for the first time in these 18 years of life, I saw a star for the first time. That genuinely felt different; maybe it was a way of the universe greeting me, patting me on my back for coming this far.
After the cake-cutting ceremony with family was over, I was back at the desk, finally opening my social media to see the wishes. I already knew that one friend who would go the extra mile to write such a loving paragraph and greet me at 12 and then end up getting worried about me not responding in time.
Then came all the other wishes of people who have been such important parts of my life at times and still continue to be.
This one day of the year, and also the results day, I see my DMs flooded. It feels lively to see how much you are cared for, but yet so ungrateful.
Then as the day slowly passed, the feeling crept in, the weight of emotions, flashbacks of life, of how grateful I am to God for making me survive all these years of life despite everything.
Well, at the end of the day things do get better, and for every bad thing that happens in life, I get something good in return—a lot better, I would say. And that is when I realize, if I had given up back then, I would not be able to cherish the joys life had offered to me eventually.
I never really understood why some people cry on their birthdays, but now I do.
Suddenly then, a notification from Google Photos pops up: 10 years ago.
And within a while, I have scrolled down to all the previous birthdays till now. Seeing the familiar faces of families, of relatives, of friends, of myself, even how I had grown up. It was almost like a film rolled on, a walk down the memory lane.
I made a vlog with my family of all the five of us cutting the cake together, and I know I will cry the next time I rewatch this video when I am 25 or something (God, I hope I make it till then). I wanted this birthday to feel perfect, to be everything I wanted for one last time, and to me it was.
I would not, however, say that it was something I could make a documentary on, maybe because it was real; it reminded me of everything one last time, of how life with time would eventually change and you would have no control over it.
Labiba Tasnim is currently studying in 12th grade at S.F.X. Greenherald International School.

Bridging the workplace divide: Moving ESP from margin to mainstream
item.description:
Think about your future dream job. Do you want to build cutting-edge software, manage global fashion brands, work in healthcare, or launch your own company right here in Bangladesh? Here’s something you should know: general classroom English just isn't enough anymore.

English is no longer just a subject you study to pass an exam or a shiny line on a resume. It has become a practical superpower that opens doors to great careers, workplace confidence, and international opportunities. Yet, there is a massive gap in Bangladesh today: what students learn in traditional English classes often doesn't match what real workplaces actually need.

Employers frequently report that fresh university graduates struggle with job-specific communication. Imagine a brilliant engineer who knows English grammar, but doesn't know how to write a technical software report, or a business graduate who can't negotiate a contract with an overseas client. The big question that teachers face today is, “Can our students actually use English to do their specific jobs well?”

To fix this gap, the Center for Language Studies at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) and TESOL-BD are teaming up for a major event: the 2nd International ESP Conference. “ESP” stands for English for Specific Purposes, which simply means teaching language tailored to real careers rather than generic textbook rules. This conference brings together university leaders, corporate bosses, teachers, and government officials to make career-focused English a core part of education across the country.

To be held on 9 October 2026 at ULAB campus, this conference will be inaugurated by the State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj at 9:00 am.  UGC member Professor Masuma Habib and Prothom Alo’s Associate Editor Anisul Hoque will be present as Special Guests. The keynote speaker will be Nigel Killick from UK, who is widely experienced in ESP field.

For years, specialised English was treated like an optional side course. But in today's fast-moving world, basic language drills won't cut it. Language is access, opportunity, and real power. To help students succeed, education needs to shift its focus from memorising textbooks to solving real workplace challenges.

To make this transformation happen, the conference is focusing on three main goals: firstly, connecting classrooms to companies; secondly showing how job-ready English skills help young people land better careers, work globally, and strengthen our national economy; and thirdly, giving practical recommendations to policymakers to make English education professionally tailored for undergraduate students.

Real change happens when everyone works together—universities listening to industries, teachers understanding job requirements, and policymakers recognising how language drives human potential. Specialised English can no longer be an afterthought in the classroom. By making job-ready English education available to every student, Bangladesh is preparing the next generation to step up, stand out, and thrive anywhere on the global stage.

ESP can no longer remain an afterthought in the classroom. By making specialised language education visible, responsive, and deeply integrated into the country's educational ecosystem, Bangladesh can empower its human capital and prepare its workforce to thrive on the global stage. This joint initiative by ULAB and TESOL BD is being organised with that very vision in mind.

Adding to this shared vision, Prothom Alo is partnering with the event as its Associate Partner.

* Shaheen Ara is an Assistant Professor at the Center for Language Studies, ULAB.

item.title: End of an era as Messi prepares to hang up Argentina boots
item.description:
SOCCER-FRIENDLY-ARG-BEN/PREVIEW

Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina's sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in a stadium with a name to match his legacy: Monumental.

Some 85,000 Argentina fans will be on hand to watch the 39-year-old idol perform his wizardry in a friendly against Benin that brings down the curtain on his 21-year international career.

Millions more will be following the action in South America's largest stadium, Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental, on TV.

The most-capped player in Argentine history is hanging up his boots two-and-a-half months after losing the World Cup final to Spain.

"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.

On Monday, he took part in his last training session with the team at the complex that bears his name in the Buenos Aires suburb of Ezeiza.

"You can't ask for more, that's it," Nahuel Nieva, a retail worker who took the day off work to watch his hero train, told AFP.

Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.

Filling the void

No effort has been spared for the sendoff of a player considered one of the game's greatest ever.

Several of the teammates with whom he reached football's pinnacle in Qatar, and who will lead the post-Messi team, will play in the game, including defender Cristian "Cuti" Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.
After the game the captain's armband will pass to Romero.

Coach Lionel Scaloni has vowed to try fill the "void" left by his talismanic captain and the signs from the next generation, some of whom weren't even alive when Messi debuted with the team in 2005, are auspicious.
In their first games since the World Cup final last week, minus Messi, Argentina thrashed Bolivia 4-0 in a friendly in Cordoba on Wednesday before running rings around Burkina Faso on Saturday at Monumental stadium.

Franco Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni, two of Argentina's brightest new hopes, both scored their first international goals against Burkina Faso in a 7-0 romp.

The results helped lift the gloom of the defeat in the World Cup final when Argentina and a visibly tired Messi were outplayed by Spain and resorted to thuggish tactics which have been punished with bans and fines for a number of players.

Coveted number 10 jersey

Messi is not only Argentina's record appearance-maker but also its leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.

"La Pulga" (The Flea) won the eternal gratitude of Argentines -- and sealed his place as rightful heir to Diego Maradona -- in 2022 when he ended their 36-year World Cup drought in Qatar.

During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina were also crowned 2005 World Youth Champions, 2008 under-23 Olympic champions and they won the Copa America in 2021 and 2024. They also won the 2022 Finalissima, a match between the champions of South America and Europe.

But there were tears along the way too, notably after Argentina's defeat by Germany in the 2014 World Cup final in Brazil, their loss to Spain in this year's final and their shock humiliation by Chile in the 2016 Copa America final.

One detail remains unclear, however: who will inherit Messi's coveted number 10 jersey?

"Until Leo's game, we won't give the number 10 to anyone," said Scaloni. "After that, we'll see."

item.title: 918 candidates did not join govt primary school
item.description:
Although the employment situation is not particularly favourable in either the public or private sector, 918 candidates, who received appointment letters for the post of assistant teacher at government primary schools, did not join their jobs.

Government jobs have long been regarded as sought after because of intense competition, benefits and job security.

However, the fact that such a large number of candidates did not join despite receiving appointment letters has raised questions.

The post of assistant teacher is at Grade 13 under the government pay scale. Under the new pay structure for 2026, the starting monthly salary, including allowances, will be at least around Tk 36,000. This makes the job more attractive in terms of pay than before.

People familiar with the matter believe that many of those who did not join may already be employed elsewhere or involved in other work. This may be the reason why they did not take up the posts despite receiving appointment letters. However, the specific reasons for their decision are not known.

In Chattogram district, 551 candidates were finally selected and recommended for appointment as assistant teachers at government primary schools. Of them, 24 did not submit the required documents. The remaining 527 submitted the documents needed to receive appointment letters. Appointment letters were issued to 525 of them, while two did not receive letters. But 64 of those who received appointment letters did not join the job.

Like Chattogram, a total of 918 candidates across 61 districts received appointment letters but did not join their jobs. 1 October was the joining date. Orientation programmes on their jobs are now being held at the upazila level for those who joined. The newly appointed teachers will be posted to schools on 11 October. Normally, those who fail to join within the stipulated period are not given another opportunity to take up the job.

Controversy over recruitment

Based on the results of the Directorate of Primary Education’s Assistant Teacher Recruitment Examination 2025, recruitment was conducted for 14,385 posts across 61 districts. A total of 14,384 candidates were finally selected based on the examination results. The Directorate of Primary Education published the final results on 8 February, at the very end of the interim government’s tenure and shortly before the national election.

Under the rules, the candidates were then supposed to undergo verification before receiving final appointments.

Initially, the district primary education offices published the list of appointed candidates on 24 September. However, it was found that the first appointment list did not include the names of a large number of candidates who had previously been recommended. Candidates who had been recommended said at the time that more than 2,000 people had been excluded.

Sources familiar with the matter said a large portion of the recommended candidates did not receive appointment letters in the first list because of negative comments from intelligence agencies. The excluded job seekers then staged protests in Dhaka, including at Shahbagh, and in various districts demanding appointments. Widespread criticism also emerged on social media.

The issue was also covered by the media. The government subsequently began gradually adding the excluded candidates to the appointment lists. Eventually, most of them received appointment letters. However, some remained excluded.

According to sources at the Directorate of Primary Education, more than 80 candidates across the 61 districts have still not been given appointment letters. Some of them are facing complications, including cases filed against them.

Those who received appointment letters were scheduled to join on 1 October. According to data from the Directorate of Primary Education, 13,831 of the selected candidates submitted the documents required for appointment as assistant teachers. Another 553 did not submit the documents. In other words, they decided not to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

Of those who submitted the required documents, 13,748 were issued appointment letters. Of them, 12,830 joined their jobs. This means 918 candidates who received appointment letters did not join. The remaining candidates did not receive appointment letters.

An official of the Directorate of Primary Education told Prothom Alo that the figure could vary by one or two.

New questions amid teacher shortage

Whether someone joins a job is a personal decision. However, the fact that so many candidates did not join could create an additional problem amid the existing teacher shortage in government primary schools. This is because it takes considerable time to complete a recruitment process and bring in new teachers.

There are 65,567 government primary schools in the country, with more than 10 million students. They have around 375,000 teachers. The teacher shortage at these schools is also growing. More than 36,000 posts of headteacher remain vacant. This means more than half of government primary schools do not have a headteacher. At the same time, several thousand posts of assistant teacher are also vacant. The lack of sufficient teachers is disrupting normal classes at many schools.

Meanwhile, following a ruling by the country’s highest court in July, the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education said it would begin the process of promoting teachers to fill the more than 36,000 vacant headteacher posts at government primary schools.

Under the current recruitment rules, 80 per cent of headteacher positions at primary schools are filled through promotion of assistant teachers, while 20 per cent are filled through direct recruitment. Therefore, if assistant teachers are promoted to fill the 36,235 vacant headteacher posts, a large number of assistant teacher positions will also become vacant.

Against this backdrop, the decision by 918 candidates to not join despite being finally recommended and receiving appointment letters adds a new dimension to the teacher shortage in primary education. At the same time, when people are struggling to find jobs amid a downturn in the labour market, the reasons why so many candidates declined government jobs after receiving them have also raised questions.

Mohammad Abdur Rahim, additional director general of the Directorate of Primary Education, told Prothom Alo that the directorate has been affected because more than 900 candidates did not join as assistant teachers.

However, whether to join a job is a matter of individual choice. It can be assumed that these candidates may have received better jobs. Many may have been pursuing several jobs at the same time. Ultimately, they chose the job they considered better. This happens, to varying degrees, in recruitment for almost all types of jobs.

item.title: Raidha Collections gets its new CEO
item.description:
Raidha Collections Ltd, one of the largest sister concerns of Labib Group has got its new chief executive officer (CEO), Shazia Zaheen Alamgir, daughter of Salahuddin Alamgir and Sultana Jahan, chairman and vice chairman of Labib Group. She has been appointed as CEO of Raidha Collections and took charge of her new role, reports a press release.

Shazia Zaheen Alamgir has been associated with the group’s business activities for a long time as group director. During her tenure as Director, she gained experience in the management and business operations of Labib Group.

For her education, she completed her MYP diploma and IB diploma from International School Dhaka (ISD). She subsequently earned her undergraduate degree from Emerson College in Boston, USA, and her postgraduate degree from City St George’s, University of London.

In her new role, Shazia Zaheen Alamgir will lead the overall business operations significantly on EU business and management of Raidha Collections. At the same time, she will work to further advance the company’s business growth and future initiatives.

In her personal life, she is married to Siraajam Munir Khan. Both are associated with City St George’s University of London. Siraajam Munir Khan is the son of Ikram Ahmed Khan, chairman of the Dubai and Hong Kong based Shun Shing Group.

Labib Group and its associates extend their warm congratulations to Shazia Zaheen Alamgir and wish her continued success in her new role.

item.title: CPJ calls for prompt investigation into attack on journalists at RU
item.description:
The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) calls on authorities to promptly and transparently investigate the 4 October attack on at least four journalists at Rajshahi University and prosecute those responsible for the violence against journalists.

The New York-based global organisation that advocates for journalists’ rights made the call in a statement issued on social media on Tuesday.

CPJ said in the statement that leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD), the student wing of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party, allegedly beat campus correspondents for The Daily Star, Samakal, bdnews24.com, and Agamir Shomoy with sticks and batons while they covered an incident outside a dormitory, according to reports. All four journalists were hospitalised.

The university filed a case against unidentified persons on 5 October, despite reports that video footage shows those involved, CPJ added.

Bangladeshi authorities must ensure journalists can report from university campuses safely and without fear of violence, and hold those responsible to account.

Three leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal — Ahsan Habib, Hasibul Islam and Bishal Chakraborty — have been expelled from the organisation in connection with the attack. Six others have been issued show-cause notices.

In the same incident, the university administration relieved Professor Mahbubur Rahman, provost of Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall, of his duties. A committee has been formed to investigate the attack.

Attack on journalists

The attack on journalists took place at around 8:30pm last Sunday in front of Shaheevcd Ziaur Rahman Hall. At least 10 people, including four journalists, were injured in the attack.

Witnesses said JCD leaders and activists went there looking for Ariful Islam, the hall's general secretary. Some of them were carrying machetes, hockey sticks, pipes and baseball bats. The journalists were attacked when they tried to record the incident.

An analysis of video footage published on social media identified seven people who directly took part in the attack. They include Ahsan Habib, vice-president of the university unit of JCD; Shariful Islam and Takbir Ahmed Emon; Hasibul Islam, joint general secretary; Shahriar Alam, assistant office secretary; Syed Sahjarul Islam, assistant general secretary; and JCD activist Bishal Chakraborty.

Bishal Chakraborty, a student of the 2021–22 academic year in the Department of Economics, is currently associated with JCD. Earlier, he was a follower of Asadullah-Hil-Galib, the general secretary of the university unit of Bangladesh Chhatra League.

item.title: Crowne Plaza Dhaka airport receives World Travel Award 2026.
item.description:
Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport has been recognised at the 33rd Annual World Travel Awards 2026, marking a significant milestone for the hotel and a proud moment for Bangladesh’s growing tourism and hospitality industry, reports a press release.

The recognition was presented during the World Travel Awards Asia, Oceania & Indian Ocean Gala Ceremony 2026, held in the Maldives on 27 September, where leading travel, tourism and hospitality organisations from across the regions gathered to celebrate industry excellence.

Established in 1993, World Travel Awards recognises excellence across the global travel, tourism and hospitality sectors and describes its recognition as the “ultimate hallmark of industry excellence.” Its annual programme brings together destinations, airlines, hotels, resorts and other leading tourism organisations from around the world.

For Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport, the achievement represents more than recognition of an individual hotel. It provides an opportunity to showcase the evolving standards and potential of Bangladesh’s tourism and hospitality industry on an international platform, alongside some of the leading travel and hospitality products from across the region.

Ashwani Nayar, cluster general manager, InterContinental Dhaka and Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport said, “This recognition is a proud milestone for Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport, but its significance goes beyond our hotel. To represent Bangladesh on a global platform alongside some of the finest names in travel, tourism and hospitality is a privilege. We believe Bangladesh has tremendous potential as a destination, and recognitions such as this help bring greater international attention to the quality, ambition and hospitality the country has to offer.”

Located strategically near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport serves business and leisure travellers while contributing to the development of Dhaka’s emerging airport hospitality ecosystem.

The recognition further strengthens the hotel’s commitment to delivering international hospitality standards while playing its part in positioning Bangladesh as an increasingly compelling destination for business, travel and tourism.

item.title: Sanctuary for birds on the rooftop
item.description:
The Dhaka Deputy Commissioner’s Office is housed in a three-storey building on Johnson Road in Old Dhaka. Tall buildings surround it on all sides, with a few trees growing in the gaps in between.

In this brick-and-concrete neighborhood, kites, pigeons, and various other birds fly across the sky in the mornings and late afternoons. Monkeys can also occasionally be spotted here.

The Dhaka district administration has taken an initiative to create a sanctuary for these birds in their rooftop.

The rooftop of the Deputy Commissioner’s Office building covers approximately 11,000 square feet. Until recently, it had remained largely unused. Now it has been furnished with fruit trees and flowering plants, water for birds to quench their thirst, birdbaths and various other amenities.

The staff of the DC Office are now waiting to see whether the birds will respond to this invitation. On 30 September from 4 pm until evening, no birds were seen on the rooftop. However, a monkey was spotted confidently walking across the roof.

People working at the office said that at other times, birds, mongooses, rabbits, squirrels, and monkeys can be seen here. But perhaps they are now hesitant to come because of the presence of people. Besides, the flowering and fruit-bearing plants have not yet grown much, and there is not much fruit on them. The animals may also not yet know what food will be available here besides honey and fruit.

However, video footage sent by the DC Office the following day showed that some birds had arrived at the rooftop garden from the surrounding area. They were seen feeding on the roof.


“Welcome to the kingdom of birds” says the slogan of the rooftop garden developed as an initiative of the Dhaka district administration. It has been named “Akashnir.”

On 16 September, Md. Moniruzzaman Mia, Commissioner of the Dhaka Division, inaugurated “Akashnir.” The initiative cost approximately 1 million taka, with support from the district administration as well as various individuals and organisations.

Farida Khanom, Dhaka Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate, told Prothom Alo, “I grew up in a village as a child, where there was the chirping of birds all around. In the city’s urban landscape of brick and concrete, that birdsong is gradually disappearing. This initiative was undertaken to bring that familiar chirping back to the city.”

Farida Khanom took charge as the DC of Dhaka on 22 April this year. She said that when she went up to the building’s rooftop to inspect the installation of solar panels, she noticed that the entire roof was lying unused. She also saw birds flying across the sky. That was when the idea of creating a safe shelter for these birds occurred to her.

The rooftop garden was subsequently developed with comprehensive support from Green Savers, a private organisation that promotes urban greening, with a particular focus on birds. One day, it will become a sanctuary for birds. They will come here without fear and feed. But that will take a little time, she said.

She described the initiative as a “small window” through which people can reconnect with nature.

The plants on the rooftop have begun spreading their branches and turning green. Various flowers have bloomed, including white hibiscus and pink bougainvillea. Fruits are beginning to appear on some of the trees, including starfruit.

According to the district administration and Green Savers, a total of 418 plants belonging to 58 species have been planted in the rooftop garden.
There are a total of 329 flowering plants here, including bougainvillea, ixora, crape jasmine, anjaliya, night-blooming jasmine, Rangoon creeper, jarul, gulmohar, kadam, kamini, hibiscus, copperpod, bakul, frangipani, gardenia, melaputiya, periwinkle, rose, canna lily, devil’s tree, and cannonball tree.

Among the aquatic flowers are water lilies and lotuses. A total of 41 fruit trees have been planted here, including lychee, starfruit, sapodilla, mango, guava, wax apple, karonda, olive, Burmese grape, hog plum, lemon, jujube, banana, papaya, cherry, and mulberry. There is also a medicinal neem tree. Other plants include nagachua, pomelia, fan palm, areca palm, China doll, cycas, variegated foliage plants, and ornamental bamboo, which will attract various insects.

The district administration has signed a three-month contract with Green Savers regarding the rooftop garden. Under the agreement, Green Savers staff will maintain the rooftop garden for these three months. After that, employees of the DC Office will take over its upkeep.
To provide birds with a safe refuge, the rooftop has been designed with artificial bamboo thickets, birdhouses, and an environment featuring trees with large canopies.

Some birds that are typically kept in cages have also been placed on the rooftop. Their chirping could be heard from the roof. DC Farida Khanom said they were kept there with the idea that birds outside would be attracted by the sound and come to the rooftop. For now, they believe these birds will serve to “invite” other birds.

According to Farida Khanom, a positive change could be brought about if, alongside government and private institutions, individuals also take initiatives to create green spaces on the rooftops of city buildings and provide a safe environment for birds.

Ahsan Rony, chief executive of Green Savers, was present at the DC's rooftop garden. He told Prothom Alo that this is a planned rooftop garden. The main message is that if city residents want to, they can turn their rooftop gardens into sanctuaries for birds. The birds can come, bathe, and feed—and then leave if they wish. They can also build nests on the rooftop if they choose.

Ahsan Rony said that the initiative at the Dhaka District Commissioner’s Office is an example of how a government institution can take steps to protect the urban environment and give special consideration to birds. Other government institutions can also be encouraged to take similar initiatives by seeing this example.

item.title: Dengue: Death toll rises to 281 as ten more die in 24 hours
item.description:
Ten people died of dengue, and 1,996 new patients were hospitalized in the country in the 24 hours until 8am on Tuesday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 281 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the new deaths, three were reported in Khulna division, two in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC), two in Barishal division, and one each was recorded in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions.
Of the total deaths recorded this year, 47.7% were men and 52.3% were women.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 90,356 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 84,299 have recovered.
According to the DGHS report, so far 75 people have died in DSCC, while 55 in Khulna division, 35 in DNCC, 25 in Chittagong division, 23 in Mymensingh, 24 in Barisal, 19 in Rajshahi, 17 in Dhaka, six in Rangpur and two in Sylhet division.

item.title: Govt plans more beds, field hospitals to tackle dengue surge
item.description:
The government has instructed all public hospitals to increase bed capacity for dengue patients and is considering setting up field hospitals to cope with the growing number of patients.
Bangla Tribune reported, citing a senior official of the Health Services Division, that the dengue hotspot areas are being prioritised for additional beds.
However, he said the field hospital plan is still under discussion.
The dengue situation is worsening rapidly, with hospital admissions rising each day. According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 1,902 new dengue patients were admitted in the 24 hours to Monday, while nine people died.
Experts said the growing number of cases is not the only concern, as the infection trend suggests the situation could worsen further.
The year’s figures show a sharp rise in hospitalisations. A total of 2,907 dengue patients were admitted in June, 9,206 in July, 20,536 in August and 43,774 in September, the highest monthly figure so far this year.
September’s admissions were 15.06 times higher than those recorded in June.
According to DGHS data, 88,360 dengue patients were hospitalised between January and October 5, compared with 48,491 during the same period last year, an increase of nearly 82%.
Deaths have also risen sharply, from 13 in June to 36 in July, 43 in August and 148 in September.
A total of 271 people have died from dengue so far this year, compared with 202 during the same period last year.
Sources said a meeting was held at the Ministry of Health on Sunday to assess the dengue situation. Following the meeting, authorities discussed measures to ease pressure on hospitals, including increasing bed capacity and setting up field hospitals.
In May, authorities took steps to establish a field hospital inside the Dhaka Medical College compound to deal with a measles outbreak. A 20-bed facility was set up with support from the Bangladesh Army.
Dhaka Medical College authorities are now considering reopening the facility to help manage the rising number of dengue patients.

item.title: Bangladesh seeks Airbus deliveries before 2030 as Biman moves to buy 10 aircraft
item.description:
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat on Tuesday stressed the need to begin deliveries of Airbus aircraft before 2030, as Bangladesh is set to sign an agreement to purchase 10 aircraft for Biman Bangladesh Airlines on Wednesday.
“We are working towards signing an agreement to purchase 10 Airbus aircraft for the development of Biman Bangladesh Airlines. However, it is essential to bring forward the delivery schedule,” the minister said, emphasizing that deliveries should begin before 2030.
He made the remarks when a Lufthansa delegation, led by German Ambassador to Bangladesh Rüdiger Lotz, paid a courtesy call on him at his ministry office at noon.
The meeting discussed air connectivity between Bangladesh and Germany, Biman’s development and other matters of mutual interest.
Millat said the longstanding friendly relations between the two countries provided considerable scope for expanding cooperation in civil aviation.
Describing Lufthansa as a globally renowned aviation company, he invited its investment in establishing maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) facilities to support Bangladesh’s ambition to become an aviation hub.
He said Lufthansa could also work with Biman to develop skilled aviation personnel within Bangladesh.
The minister sought Germany’s cooperation in securing the withdrawal of the European Union’s High Risk Cargo and Mail (HRCM) designation for cargo originating from Bangladesh, which has remained in place since 2017.
He said the government had taken measures to address all observations since assuming office.
Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and Osmani International Airport each achieved ratings exceeding 90% in recently completed security audits, he said, citing the results while seeking German support for lifting the designation.
Both sides expressed interest in deepening bilateral relations, increasing air connectivity and expanding cooperation in tourism.
Millat expressed optimism that cooperation between Bangladesh and Germany would become broader and more fruitful in the coming years.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir stresses stronger UN coordination, alignment with Bangladesh reform framework
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Tuesday called for stronger coordination among UN agencies and closer alignment of UN programmes with Bangladesh’s Five-Year Strategic Framework for Reform and Development (2026-2031).
“Bangladesh highly values its longstanding partnership with the United Nations and remains committed to further reinforcing its cooperation in support of shared priorities and national development,” he said during a meeting with Carol Flore-Smereczniak, UN resident coordinator ad interim, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The state minister expressed appreciation to Flore-Smereczniak for her leadership of the UN Country Team in advancing Bangladesh’s development priorities.
In response to a query, State Minister Kobir shared a brief overview of the prime minister’s key engagements during the recently concluded High-Level Week of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, including the meeting with the UN Secretary-General.
On the Rohingya crisis, the state minister appreciated the UN’s humanitarian support and called for sustained UN efforts to ensure the early and sustainable return of the Rohingyas to their ancestral homes in Myanmar, emphasizing that repatriation remains the only viable solution.
The UN resident coordinator ad interim lauded the Government’s ongoing support and reaffirmed the UN’s readiness to deepen its partnership with Bangladesh.
She also underscored the UN Country Team’s commitment to working closely with the government to address shared challenges.

item.title: 4 new subjects to be introduced in class-VI curriculum from 2027
item.description:
Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon on Tuesday said four new subjects will be introduced in the Class VI curriculum from 2027.
“The new subjects are joyful learning, technical education, sports and culture. The four new subjects are being introduced in Class Six from 2027,” he said.
The minister made the announcement while responding to questions from journalists after inaugurating the 53rd National Summer Sports Competition at the Bhasha Shoinik Shaheed Dhirendranath Datta Stadium, Comilla, on Tuesday morning.
He said students need to be engaged in creativity, technical skills, sports and cultural activities alongside their academic studies from an early age.
The minister also said the curriculum would be changed and revised as necessary from 2028.
The government would also consider adding more books to the curriculum based on students’ needs and the demands of the times, he added.
Speaking as a special guest at the event, Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin said the ongoing war in the Middle East had pushed up international prices of gas and fuel oil, affecting Bangladesh as well.
However, diesel prices in Bangladesh remain comparatively lower than in neighbouring and other surrounding countries, he said.
He said Bangladesh was providing higher subsidies on fuel than other countries in an effort to keep prices affordable.
The government is making every effort to address the crisis caused by the global situation, he added.
Mahdi Amin said the current crisis was not confined to any single country but was a global crisis.
He said the government was working to address the situation in a rational manner while keeping in mind the need to minimise the burden on the people.
Housing and Public Works Minister Zakaria Taher and Comilla-10 constituency lawmaker Md Mobasher Alam Bhuiyan were also present, among others.
Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education Bangladesh, Dhaka, Prof Dr Khan Moinuddin Al Mahmud Sohel chaired the event.
Students from schools, madrasas and technical education institutions under various education boards across Bangladesh are participating in the 53rd Summer National Sports Competition.

item.title: DMP: Tight security planned across Dhaka for Durga Puja
item.description:
Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed has said tight security measures will be in place across the capital during Durga Puja.
“Every puja mandap will be secured with the utmost vigilance to ensure peaceful celebrations,” he said at a meeting on security, law and order and traffic management at DMP headquarters on Tuesday.
He said security measures would remain in place from Mahalaya through the festival and idol immersion. All puja mandaps will be covered by CCTV cameras, while mandap officials will use body cameras.
Uniformed and plainclothes police will be deployed, with SWAT, Crisis Response Team, Quick Response Team, crime scene vans and bomb disposal units kept on standby, he said.
The commissioner urged puja committees to monitor volunteers and visitors and contact 999 or the nearest police station in case of emergencies.
Puja committee leaders sought DMP’s cooperation in ensuring security and smooth traffic management during the festival.

item.title: Govt plans ‘Shishu Swargo’ centres for children with cerebral palsy
item.description:
The government is set to set up "Shishu Swargo" centers across 22 districts this fiscal year to provide integrated medical and rehabilitation services to children living with cerebral palsy (CP), State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit announced on Tuesday.
Speaking as the chief guest at an event marking World Cerebral Palsy Day at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital (NINS) in Agargaon, the minister highlighted the critical gap in existing healthcare coverage for children with neurological conditions.
Citing research data, Dr Muhit noted that at least 350,000 children in Bangladesh live with cerebral palsy, yet NINS—the country's apex neurological institution—could treat only 3,300 children in its outpatient department last year.
Children living with cerebral palsy, alongside parents, doctors, and disability rights advocates, participate in a rally marking World Cerebral Palsy Day outside the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital (NINS) in Agargaon, Dhaka on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
"The vast majority of these children remain essentially invisible, isolated at home due to family limitations and social stigma," Dr Muhit said. "As a state, we are committed to restoring their rights and dignity."
Following directives from the prime minister, the health sector has received prioritized budgetary support, facilitating the establishment of these specialized district care centers, he added.
Dr Muhit also highlighted a pilot program recently launched in the Korail slum area, where around 300 identified children are currently receiving specialized care.
Participants in a rally marking World Cerebral Palsy Day outside the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital (NINS) in Agargaon, Dhaka on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Emphasizing early intervention, the state minister stressed the need for community-based early case detection systems to identify pediatric neurological disorders in rural and underserved communities.
State Minister for Housing and Public Works Ahmed Sohel Manjur also addressed the program as a special guest, alongside senior health officials and medical specialists.

item.title: Minister: Fisheries budget must rise while curbing waste
item.description:
Fisheries, Livestock and Agriculture Minister Mohammed Amin Ur Rashid has called for increased budget allocations for the fisheries sector alongside greater transparency, accountability and stronger measures to prevent financial waste.
He made the remarks on Tuesday while speaking as the chief guest at a workshop titled “Budget and Government Development Vision in the Fisheries Sector”, organised by the Department of Fisheries at Matsya Bhaban in Dhaka.
The minister said the country’s identity as “Mache-Bhate Bangali” is deeply connected with the fisheries sector, but the availability of native fish species has declined due to the shrinking of natural water bodies and environmental changes.
He said: “Therefore, alongside boosting production, priority must be given to preserving the natural habitats of fish.”
Emphasising the importance of fish sanctuaries, Amin Ur Rashid said launching projects and spending funds alone would not ensure their effectiveness. He called for regular field-level verification to assess whether sanctuaries are achieving their intended objectives.
“The primary purpose of sanctuaries is to create opportunities for fish breeding and reproduction,” he said, adding that regular reviews were needed to determine how funds were spent, what was achieved and how the initiatives affected overall fish production.
The minister also urged officials to ensure accuracy in the lists of fishermen eligible for government support.
He warned that the inclusion of fake or ineligible beneficiaries could deprive genuine fishermen of government assistance and called on local officials to take greater responsibility during the verification process.
On deep-sea fishing, the minister said Bangladesh has significant potential to commercially harvest tuna and other marine resources in international waters, as several countries are already doing so.
“Instead of merely conducting surveys and spending money, a clear plan is required to translate survey findings into actual marine harvesting,” he said.
He stressed the need to develop skilled manpower, suitable vessels and technological capacity to utilise the country’s deep-sea fishing potential.
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku, speaking as the special guest, stressed the need to encourage young entrepreneurs and provide fish farmers with necessary advice and technical support.
He also instructed field-level officials to conduct regular farm inspections and monitor activities.
The state minister said the government is working to increase freshwater fish production, expand exports and bring canals, rivers and other water bodies under fish cultivation.
He identified pollution-free water bodies, maintaining river navigability, improving fish processing facilities and promoting exports as important factors for the sustainable development of the fisheries sector.
Department of Fisheries Director General Dr Md Khaled Kanak chaired the workshop.
Ministry Secretary Md Delwar Hossain attended the event as the honoured guest, while Public Service Commission Member Prof A S M Golam Hafiz participated as the discussant.
Senior officials from the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock and the Department of Fisheries were also present.

item.title: Editors’ Council calls for end to attacks on journalists
item.description:
The Editors’ Council has expressed deep concern and strongly condemned recent attacks, threats, harassment and obstruction of journalists in different parts of Bangladesh.
The council said the latest attack on journalists at Rajshahi University, while they were performing their professional duties, is particularly concerning. The journalists were collecting information and reporting in the public interest, not on behalf of any particular side.
There is no justification for attacking, threatening, or obstructing journalists, even when there are disagreements over a report, opinion, or a journalist’s professional activities, it added.
“An attack on a journalist is not only an attack on a professional; it is an attack on independent journalism, freedom of expression and the public’s right to know,” it said.
The Editors’ Council welcomed the filing of a case and the initiative to investigate the Rajshahi University incident.
However, it said the investigation must be impartial, credible and evidence-based, and those involved in the attack must be brought to justice regardless of their political or organisational affiliations.
