The Editors’ Council said journalists’ safety is not a special privilege but an essential condition for a free, democratic and accountable society.
“Independent journalism is not possible in an environment of fear, threats and violence,” it said, calling on the government, law enforcement agencies, political parties, educational institutions and all relevant stakeholders to take prompt, visible and lawful action in every incident of attack on journalists and adopt effective measures to prevent such incidents in the future.

item.title: PM: Strong children mean a stronger Bangladesh
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Tuesday likened children to the strong pillars of a house, saying Bangladesh’s foundation would become stronger in the competitive world if every child is given the opportunity to develop their abilities properly.
“Children are the pillars of their families. When children are given the right environment and opportunities to grow and flourish, families become stronger,” he while addressing a program marking Children’s Rights Day, 2026 and the 50th anniversary of Bangladesh Shishu Academy on the academy premises in the capital.
In the same way, Tarique said: “If we can ensure opportunities for every child across Bangladesh to develop their full potential, the foundation of our country will become much stronger, enabling Bangladesh to emerge as a strong country in the competitive world.”
He said the government wants to develop children in a way that strengthens their future, as the strength of today’s children will determine the strength of the nation’s future.
“We want to develop our children in a way that makes their future strong. A strong future for today’s children means a strong future for the nation. And a strong future for the nation means we will be able to build a strong and powerful Bangladesh,” the Prime Minister said.
Tarique urged children to develop themselves not only through education but also through sports, Quran recitation, music and other cultural activities.
“You have to become good human beings,” he said, urging children to properly develop the qualities and talents within them.
The prime minister also called on children to be kind to all living beings and caring towards nature and the environment. “People should show kindness not only to other people but also to nature and all of its creations.”
He urged children to care for trees around their homes and schools and to be kind to birds and animals, describing them as national assets.
Tarique also called on guardians to help children develop a sense of responsibility towards nature from an early age.
“If we are kind to nature, nature will also be kind to us,” he said, urging children and guardians to work together to protect the environment.
The prime minister also asked children to play a role in keeping their surroundings clean. He urged them to politely remind adults not to throw waste indiscriminately and to use designated places for disposing of rubbish.
“If we can build a clean and beautiful environment today, your children will grow up in a healthy environment, both physically and mentally,” he said.
The prime minister said the government is working to provide children across the country with opportunities to develop their talents in sports, arts, culture and music, particularly because many families cannot afford such facilities.
He said the government has recently organised a football competition at the primary-school level in which around 2.2 million children — 1.1 million boys and 1.1 million girls — participated.
“If we can continue this, I firmly believe that one day a Pele or internationally recognised players will emerge from among our children,” he said.
The prime minister also recalled the “Notun Kuri” program introduced by Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman to nurture children’s cultural talents, saying the government has revived it while also launching similar initiatives in sports.
He said sports activities have also been initiated alongside cultural programs, with events being organised at the national level.
“We want our children to have good exposure to art, culture and music, while also becoming capable in sports,” Tarique said, adding that every child has some quality or talent that needs to be given an opportunity to flourish.
The prime minister said the government is working to introduce facilities at schools so that children, including those in remote and rural areas, can choose activities according to their interests.
He said the government plans to provide opportunities from the primary and secondary levels for children to learn music, play musical instruments and participate in different sports.
“We want to develop children in this way to make their future stronger,” the Prime Minister said.
Tarique also announced plans to introduce opportunities for children to learn a third foreign language alongside Bangla and English.
He said students would be able to choose from several languages, potentially including Arabic, Mandarin and German, to help them in higher education and employment abroad.
“Learning a third foreign language will help them stand firmly in life and compete with people from other countries,” Tarique said.
The prime minister, however, stressed that academic achievement, sports, cultural activities or learning several languages alone would not be enough.“Dear little friends, you have many responsibilities. You have to be humane,” he said.
Earlier, around 150 children welcomed the prime minister when he arrived at Bangladesh Shishu Academy. The program began with the national anthem.
Prime minister’s wife and Ziaur Rahman Foundation Vice-Chairman Dr Zubaida Rahman attended the program, chaired by Women and Children Affairs Minister Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain.
The prime minister enjoyed cultural performances by children and later interacted with the performers and took part in a photo session. He also answered questions from children.
Children from different parts of the country also interacted with the prime minister through videoconference.
Tarique later visited an exhibition of paintings by children and a photo gallery at the Children’s Museum building and inaugurated a solar panel system and a substation on its ground floor.
Earlier, children presented him with a commemorative gift, while he unveiled the special souvenir Shaishab.
This year’s program is being held under the theme “Let every child have a secure future.”

item.title: Dhanmondi Lake restoration begins, 'Nazrul Sarobar' in plan
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has begun dredging Dhanmondi Lake as part of an extensive development program aimed at restoring its navigability, environmental quality and recreational facilities.
The dredging work was inaugurated on Tuesday morning by DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam and Road Transport and Bridges Minister and local lawmaker Sheikh Rabiul Alam.
The 3.10-km-long lake has an average width of 56 metres and an estimated 162,534 cubic metres of accumulated sludge, including mud and waste.
Two floating excavators and four barges will be used to remove around 700 cubic metres of sludge daily. The dredging is expected to take about a year and initially cost Tk26 crore.
The site covers around 86 acres, including about 55 acres of water body. The lake was developed in the 1960s from the remnants of the old Pandu River.
Speaking at the inauguration, Sheikh Rabiul Alam said the development and management of Dhanmondi Lake had been one of his election pledges.
“The prime minister has approved two projects in this regard. As the first phase, sludge removal from the lake began today (Tuesday). The entire lake will be renovated according to the detailed design,” he said.
He also urged visitors and local residents to remain conscious of their responsibility to protect the lake’s environment.
DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam said several development works would begin after the lakebed is cleaned.
“Immediately after cleaning the lakebed, water treatment, sidewall renovation, modernisation and expansion of the walkway, beautification and lighting works will begin,” he said.
He said facilities including speedboat rides for children would also be introduced, while roads, footpaths and other infrastructure in the Dhanmondi area would be improved.
An open cultural and recreational centre named “Nazrul Sarobar”, modelled on Rabindra Sarobar, will also be developed as part of the initiative.
The DSCC has prepared a Tk75 crore master plan to restore Dhanmondi Lake and develop it as a recreational destination while addressing long-standing waterlogging, infrastructure and environmental problems.
Of the total allocation, Tk50 crore has been earmarked for renovating the lake and related infrastructure, while Tk25 crore will be spent on the proposed “Nazrul Sarobar” or “Bidrohi Chattar”.
The wider plan includes strengthening the lake’s banks and stabilising its slopes, improving drainage, renovating walkways and repairing boundary fencing and safety railings.
It also includes improved lighting, CCTV cameras, a public announcement system and directional signboards.
The master plan proposes three floating decks, kiosks, a modern gym, cafeteria, badminton court, open-air gymnasium and parking facilities.
It also includes a specialised “tree hospital” for plant maintenance, safe drinking water facilities and public toilets.
The proposed Nazrul Sarobar will be developed on 50.967 kathas of land beside Road 13/A and Road 8/A in Dhanmondi, opposite the Kazi Nazrul Islam Institute.
The Tk25 crore cultural space will feature an open-air amphitheatre and green room for Nazrul songs, cultural programs and discussions.
It will also include a book corner, library, information panels, urban forest, plaza and a lake ghat highlighting the life, literary works and rebellious spirit of National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam.
A restaurant and café serving some of Nazrul’s favourite foods are also planned.
According to the development plan, the main lake renovation and construction of Nazrul Sarobar will be carried out simultaneously after sludge removal is completed.
The authorities expect the project to address the lake’s long-standing environmental and infrastructure problems while creating a safer and more accessible recreational and cultural space in one of Dhaka’s major urban areas.

item.title: DCs ordered to ensure LPG, autogas sales at BERC-set prices
item.description:
All deputy commissioners (DCs) have been instructed to take necessary measures to keep LPG supplies normal in the open market and ensure that LPG and autogas are sold at the prices set by the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC), said Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday.
The government has intensified monitoring across the country to ensure the sale of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and autogas at prices fixed by the commission amid volatility in international fuel prices, he said at a press briefing held at the Secretariat on the progress of various government activities.
Fuel prices in the international market remain highly volatile, while the government is trying to adjust LPG prices accordingly, he said adding “However, there have been complaints that LPG is not available at the adjusted prices in some places,” he said.
The energy and mineral resources minister held an online meeting with the DCs and issued necessary directives in this regard, he added.
Monitoring is also being conducted in different districts through mobile courts operated by the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection and local administrations, he said.
“Earlier, many were fined. Now, these monitoring activities have been intensified further,” the adviser said.
The government is also holding discussions with LPG traders to improve the market situation, he said.
The energy minister has held several meetings with leaders of LPG-related businesses to review the situation, Zahed said, adding that the traders assured the minister of their cooperation in keeping the market stable.
The government hopes the current crisis in the LPG market will ease through these efforts, he said.
Zahed urged the media to highlight any complaints about LPG not being available at the government-fixed prices.
“If LPG is still unavailable at the fixed price anywhere, the media will highlight the issue in the public interest, and the government will take necessary action. LPG is an extremely essential product. In fact, it is not possible to manage without it,” the adviser said.

item.title: Expelled Jubo Dal leader Simon sent to jail in Banglamotor shooting case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent expelled Jubo Dal leader Ferdous Ahmed Simon to jail after he completed a four-day remand in a case filed over an alleged attack and firing of blank shots in the capital’s Banglamotor area following an extortion demand.
After completing his four-day remand, Hatirjheel Police Station Sub-Inspector Md Nasim and also the investigating officer in the case, produced the accused before the court on Tuesday and sought an order to keep him in jail.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jewel Rana passed the order following the prosecution’s plea.
Sub-Inspector Arif Reza of the prosecution division confirmed the matter.
He said three other accused were sent to jail on Monday after completing three-day remands, while Simon was sent to jail on Tuesday after completing his four-day remand.
According to the prosecution, Simon provided important information during his remand, which investigators are now verifying. Police also said he could go into hiding if granted bail and that keeping him in custody was necessary for a proper investigation.
On October 2, the court granted different periods of remand for Simon and three others, Omar, 32, Morshed, 25, and Md Shawon, 25.
According to the case statement, the accused stopped complainant Md Sohan in front of a house in the New Eskaton area of Banglamotor under Hatirjheel Police Station around 7:15pm on October 1.
The complaint alleged that Simon demanded Tk50,000 from Sohan. When Sohan refused, Simon allegedly pulled out a pistol, pointed it at Sohan’s chest and attempted to fire.
Simon then allegedly struck Sohan on the head with the butt of the pistol, while the other accused also assaulted him.
The accused left the scene after local residents intervened, according to the complaint.
Sohan received initial treatment at a nearby pharmacy before heading for further medical care.

item.title: Govt considering dengue vaccination in long term
item.description:
The government is considering introducing a dengue vaccine as a long-term measure to reduce infections and deaths, but there are no immediate plans to vaccinate people against dengue, State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit said on Tuesday.
“We are discussing vaccines as a long-term measure. There are probably three dengue vaccine candidates in the world at present. We are also considering the issue in Bangladesh, but it is not happening at this moment,” he said.
The state minister made the remarks at a seminar on tackling the dengue crisis at Holy Family Red Crescent Medical College Hospital in Dhaka. The Doctors Association of Bangladesh (DAB) organised the event.
Dr Muhit said Bangladesh has all dengue variants, describing it as a “unique scientific finding.”
He said while one or two variants are generally dominant in many countries, all variants have been detected in Bangladesh.
Referring to his recent visit to Japan, he said the country also has a dengue vaccine candidate and Bangladesh is discussing the issue. However, further research and trials are needed before any decision is made on vaccination.
Dr Muhit stressed prevention as the main way to reduce dengue infections and deaths, particularly by eliminating Aedes mosquito breeding grounds.
He said public participation is essential to destroy mosquito larvae, as neither the government nor any single organisation can keep the entire country clean.
Clean-up drives are underway in neighbourhoods, educational institutions and government offices, while local government bodies are working to destroy mosquito larvae and control mosquitoes, he added.
The government is also focusing on early diagnosis, prompt referral and improved treatment for infected patients, Dr Muhit said.
He said around 2,000 doctors across the country have received updated training in dengue management over the past two months.
A clinical management guideline for dengue patients is also being circulated with support from the Society of Medicine.
“Good clinical management after infection can reduce the death rate,” he said.

item.title: End of an era as Messi prepares to hang up Argentina boots
item.description:
Lionel Messi will pull on Argentina's sky blue-and-white jersey for the last time on Tuesday and enjoy an emotional farewell in front of his adoring fans in a stadium with a name to match his legacy: Monumental.
Some 85,000 Argentina fans will be on hand to watch the 39-year-old idol perform his wizardry in a friendly against Benin that brings down the curtain on his 21-year international career.
Millions more will be following the action in South America's largest stadium, Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental, on TV.
The most-capped player in Argentine history is hanging up his boots two-and-a-half months after losing the World Cup final to Spain.
"I gave it my all; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are great young players coming up who deserve their chance," Messi wrote when announcing his international retirement in August.
On Monday, he took part in his last training session with the team at the complex that bears his name in the Buenos Aires suburb of Ezeiza.
"You can't ask for more, that's it," Nahuel Nieva, a retail worker who took the day off work to watch his hero train, told AFP.
Messi remains under contract with Inter Miami until 2028, although following the death of his father, Jorge, two months ago, he revealed he may hang up his boots for good sooner than anticipated.
- Filling the void -
No effort has been spared for the sendoff of a player considered one of the game's greatest ever.
Several of the teammates with whom he reached football's pinnacle in Qatar, and who will lead the post-Messi team, will play in the game, including defender Cristian "Cuti" Romero, midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Enzo Fernandez and forwards Julian Alvarez and Lautaro Martinez.
After the game the captain's armband will pass to Romero.
Coach Lionel Scaloni has vowed to try fill the "void" left by his talismanic captain and the signs from the next generation, some of whom weren't even alive when Messi debuted with the team in 2005, are auspicious.
In their first games since the World Cup final last week, minus Messi, Argentina thrashed Bolivia 4-0 in a friendly in Cordoba on Wednesday before running rings around Burkina Faso on Saturday at Monumental stadium.
Franco Mastantuono and Gianluca Prestianni, two of Argentina's brightest new hopes, both scored their first international goals against Burkina Faso in a 7-0 romp.
The results helped lift the gloom of the defeat in the World Cup final when Argentina and a visibly tired Messi were outplayed by Spain and resorted to thuggish tactics which have been punished with bans and fines for a number of players.
Coveted number 10 jersey Messi is not only Argentina's record appearance-maker but also its leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 games, as well as a record 68 assists.
"La Pulga" (The Flea) won the eternal gratitude of Argentines -- and sealed his place as rightful heir to Diego Maradona -- in 2022 when he ended their 36-year World Cup drought in Qatar.
During his time with the Albiceleste, Argentina were also crowned 2005 World Youth Champions, 2008 under-23 Olympic champions and they won the Copa America in 2021 and 2024. They also won the 2022 Finalissima, a match between the champions of South America and Europe.
But there were tears along the way too, notably after Argentina's defeat by Germany in the 2014 World Cup final in Brazil, their loss to Spain in this year's final and their shock humiliation by Chile in the 2016 Copa America final.
One detail remains unclear, however: who will inherit Messi's coveted number 10 jersey?
"Until Leo's game, we won't give the number 10 to anyone," said Scaloni. "After that, we'll see."

item.title: Hasan Mahmud: Test cricket momentum turning for Bangladesh
item.description:
Fast-rising pace bowler Hasan Mahmud said on Monday Bangladesh's upward trajectory has made a place in the World Test Championship final a realistic dream for his team.
Bangladesh are fourth in the World Test Championship standings after a shock nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin in August, a result that highlighted the strides made by a side long regarded as Test underachievers.
"The momentum is coming towards us, definitely," Hasan, 26, told AFP in an interview in Dhaka.
"The atmosphere is such that Bangladesh can now dominate in Test cricket," said the right-arm bowler, who played a key role by taking 6-55 in Darwin.
"We haven't dominated (in Test cricket). Now is the time."
Hasan said the Darwin victory could be a springboard for bigger achievements for Bangladesh, who have won six of their 13 Tests in the past two years.
Bangladesh have six Tests remaining in the current World Test Championship cycle, including home series against the West Indies and England, as well as a tour of South Africa.
"If we win four matches at home, why shouldn't we play in the World Test Championship final? That's the dream for Bangladesh now," Hasan said.
The paceman, who enjoyed a successful county stint with Kent this year, has been a central figure in Bangladesh's recent rise.
Nicknamed "Mini-McGrath" after the Australian great Glenn McGrath, he believes the perception of Bangladeshi pace bowling is changing as the South Asian country produces a new generation of quicks.
"Since we started playing, the thinking has changed," he said.
"They now realise Bangladesh also has good-quality fast bowlers who can be world-class."
Hasan's aggressive approach was evident during the Australia series, where he focused on building pressure on batsmen.
"I was just doing my job and bowling. I wasn't giving them anything easy to hit. I would attack them with the short ball and keep bowling my way. If they hit me, they hit me," he said.
Bangladesh were unable to clinch the two-Test series, with Australia claiming the second Test in Mackay by an innings and 51 runs.
However, Hasan said he was confident that Bangladesh's "graph will continue to move upward" in the coming days.
"Look at how much we've improved in Test cricket," he said.
"If the fast bowlers stay in good shape and the batsmen remain in form, then we will go to a higher level."

item.title: France roar back in Nations League as Italy beat Turkey
item.description:
Michael Olise starred as France stormed back from behind to thrash Belgium 4-1 in the UEFA Nations League on Monday, while Italy continued their resurgence with victory over Turkey.
Dodi Lukebakio's first-half strike had Belgium on track for a first competitive victory over France since 1981, but Zinedine Zidane turned to his star-studded bench and the hosts produced a devastating late surge.
Les Bleus struck four times in the final 13 minutes to keep Zidane's unbeaten record as coach intact as France edged closer to a place in the quarter-finals.
Desire Doue equalised with a low shot from the edge of the box before Olise pulled the ball back for Rayan Cherki to put France ahead as the floodgates opened, with substitutes accounting for all of the hosts' goals.
Olise put the game to bed with a scruffy third goal before he grabbed another in stoppage time to round off a breathtaking turnaround.
"I think we played well at the end. The first half was difficult.. but we kept going and we're happy," Olise told TF1.
The Bayern Munich winger has been France's most influential player in the early stages of Zidane's reign, netting four times in his last three matches despite starting only once.
"It's a team effort. He (Zidane) brings his own ideas and we follow him. We've done well in these four games and we'll keep going," said Olise.
France hold a three-point lead over Italy in Group A1, with Belgium another point behind.
Zidane's team will complete their group campaign with games away to Italy and at home to Turkey next month.
Italy, who are rebuilding under Roberto Mancini, moved up into second place courtesy of a 3-1 win over Turkey in Bologna.
Gianluca Scamacca drilled Italy ahead only for Aral Simsir to level just after the hour. The Azzurri, who thrashed Turkey 4-1 last week in Bursa, secured another win at home with goals from Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito.
"There was fatigue all around, and we struggled a bit. But we did well to score, and then to score again right after they equalised," said Mancini.
The 61-year-old, who led Italy to Euro 2020 glory, is back for a second spell in charge of a nation who have failed to qualify for the last three World Cups.
"We have to keep playing. We're currently in second place, and we'll likely have to fight to secure that spot in Belgium," added Mancini.
Northern Ireland remain top of Group B2 but had to settle for a 0-0 draw against Georgia after Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili saved a late Isaac Price penalty in Belfast.
Hungary are a point adrift following a 2-1 win over Ukraine in a match played in Slovakia.
Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres scored for the seventh Nations League game in a row to give Sweden a 1-0 win in Romania. Graham Potter's side sit two points clear in Group B4 of Bosnia and Herzegovina, who beat Poland 1-0.
Former Tottenham winger Marcus Edwards scored a stoppage-time winner as Cyprus edged Latvia 2-1 in Group C2, while leaders Montenegro and Armenia drew 0-0.

item.title: Coco Gauff calls out online racism following China open video review
item.description:
American tennis star Coco Gauff said Tuesday she faced an "insane" amount of online racist abuse after defeating Chinese teenager Sun Xinran in a match that included a video review.
During Monday's China Open match against 16-year-old Sun Xinran in Beijing, the former US Open champion requested a video review over flickering LED lights, prompting some boos from the crowd.
"Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist," Gauff wrote on X.
"The amount of racist comments and messages I've received in the last few hours is insane," her post read.
The umpire agreed for the point to be replayed, and 22-year-old Gauff went on to win the match 7-5, 6-1.
Responding on X to a post containing a racial slur that was flagged as potential "hateful content", the Black American player clarified in a separate post that she challenged the point before Sun's return when she noticed the lights flicker a second time.
"I think it's weird I'm getting hate for following the rules," she said, explaining that players are instructed they can challenge points after play has concluded.
"Xinran is an incredible talent and player. I apologised for the situation at the end of the match, and she completely understood," she added.
By Tuesday morning, the hashtag "Gauff apologised to Sun Xinran after the match" had hit 4.5 million views, ranking as the sixth top trend on Chinese social media platform Weibo.
The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) did not immediately respond to AFP.
During a quarter-final match between Alexander Zverev and Novak Djokovic in the men's draw on Sunday, the umpire also agreed to replay a point after Zverev complained about flickering panels.
Gauff, the world No. 4, claimed the Beijing title in 2024. She is due to play Belgium's Elise Mertens in the round of 16 on Wednesday.

item.title: Ebadot's strategy to combat UAE heat
item.description:
Bangladesh fast bowler Ebadot Hossain stressed the importance of starting preparations well before the match day in a bid to combat the extreme heat of the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
Bangladesh are now in Dubai to play a two-day warm-up match against the UAE as part of their preparation for the one-off Test against Afghanistan.
Abu Dhabi, however, will host the Test match. But the heat is more or less the same in every place in the UAE.
However, Ebadot said they are careful of tackling the heat since the dehydration caused by excessive sweating can lead to muscle cramps and make it difficult for pacers to maintain their intensity for long periods in hot conditions.
"My preparation is to stay hydrated, take more water, fluids, coconut water or fruits two days before the match," Ebadot shared in a video released by the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB).
"In such heat, there is a lot of sweating. So if I am dehydrated during the match day, it can help maintain my bowling rhythm."
The fast bowler said adapting his body to the conditions is an important part of his match preparation, particularly before Test matches.
"You cannot bowl for a long time in the heat. It is actually a matter of preparation," he said. "So my match preparation starts two days in advance, especially for Test matches when condition is such unforgiving." Ebadot also urged younger cricketers visiting the UAE to familiarize themselves with the local weather before arriving.
He said players from Bangladesh, including those representing the Under-19 and emerging teams, should learn about the temperature and humidity in advance so they can prepare accordingly.
"First know the conditions, how the humidity or how hot it is here," Ebadot said, noting that temperatures in the UAE can become extremely high during the summer months.
Ebadot said he follows an unusual practice that he believes helps him acclimatize quickly. On his first practice day, he walks barefoot on the ground for about an hour.
"What I do after coming here is, when I come on the first practice day, I stay barefoot with this ground for an hour," he said, adding, "The connection with the ground would help you adjust. I found it very helpful as the body adapts to this weather quickly."

item.title: Bangladesh U19 Women’s suffer defeat in last ball tragedy
item.description:
Bangladesh Under-19 Women’s team tasted a heartbreaking four-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka in the last-ball thriller in a Tri-nation series in Faisalabad Pakistan today.
The defeat came after they beat hosts Pakistan U19 Women’s team by 30 runs in the first match.
Opting to bat first, Bangladesh amassed 119-7 in their 20-over allocation with captain Sadia Islam top-scoring for the side with 22 ball-39.
Bangladesh, however, made Sri Lanka toiling hard before conceding the defeat in the last ball, as Sri Lanka reached 120-6.
Bangladesh made a horrible start to the innings losing opener Mymuna Naher and Achen Jannat cheaply before Bibi Ayesha was dismissed for duck, leaving the side at precarious 28-3 in eighth over.
Nishita Akter Nishi and captain Sadia Islam then steadied the innings with 56-run for the fourth wicket, which eventually paved the way to go past 100 plus score.
Nishi made 26 before being trapped run out.
The late order batters failed to capitalize on Sadia and Nishi’s partnership as Bangladesh failed to post a substantial score.
But the bowlers showed a never-say-die attitude to make the contest evenly. They struck back at regular intervals, keeping Sri Lanka at bay.
Opener Sanjana Kavindi kept the side in the hunt amid inspirational bowling from Bangladesh bowlers and scored 48 off 46 before being dismissed.
Her innings eventually was instrumental in taking the game to the last over where Danodya Sewmini and Limanasa Thilakarathna held the nerve to seal the deal in the last ball.
Nishi claimed 2-26 for Bangladesh but her stellar all-round performance eventually went in vain.

item.title: ‘Afraid for my future:’ Tens of thousands demand better education in France
item.description:
Tens of thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Tuesday, as unions and teachers joined high school students who for days have been demanding better learning conditions in protests punctuated by violent confrontations.
Students have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds since late September, complaining of missing teachers, overloaded timetables, dilapidated classrooms and buildings that cannot cope with rising temperatures.
Unions, rights groups and the children have accused the authorities of using disproportionate force -- a police stun grenade tore the hand off one teenager on Monday and another youngster had his teeth knocked out last week after police fired a grenade launcher at his head.
“I’m afraid for my future,” Selma, 15, told AFP without giving her surname, among the thousands marching in the country’s second largest city of Marseille.
The unrest has erupted with just months to go before the 2027 election to choose a successor to centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with far-right veteran candidate Marine Le Pen riding high in the polls despite a graft conviction.
“We just want to save our education and be educated,” said Oceanne, 18, also at the protest in the southern port city.
She said she had suffered from absent teachers who were either not replaced or replaced by “pointless substitutes.”
Another student held up a sign complaining of long hours at school.
“Timetables as packed as Le Pen’s criminal record,” it read, in a jab at the far-right presidential hopeful.
A major march was set to depart from central Paris in the early afternoon.
The interior ministry said 86,000 had already joined demonstrations across the rest of the country earlier Tuesday. The CGT union put that figure at 260,000 people.
In Rennes, in western France, teacher Romain Dubourg said he and other teachers were present outside the Chateaubriand high school to show support.
“With about thirty colleagues, we talked about the police brutality we’ve witnessed and decided to be there for our students if they need us,” he told AFP.
While many protests have been peaceful, some demonstrators have started fires, destroyed bus shelters or clashed with riot police.
Police have responded with batons, tear gas and riot-control rounds.
The government says 215 students and 715 police officers have been injured since the start of the movement.
A 15-year-old lost a hand to a sting-ball grenade fired by riot officers in the northern town of Lens on Monday.
“It’s scary,” said Mike Ryan, 16, who decided against joining protests in Lens after seeing the images on social media.
“A hand cut off like that, it feels like we’re at war,” he told AFP.
The prosecutor’s office in the northeastern town of Metz meanwhile said he called for a police inquiry over a possible sexual assault on a minor younger than 15, after video footage circulated of what appeared to be a plainclothes policeman groping a female pupil he had detained.
The government has sought to address the grievances, while accusing the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of being behind the movement.
Veteran LFI presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has strongly supported the protests, while calling for non-violent methods.
The head of the CGT labor union Sophie Binet has said its members would be there to “protect high school students.”
Greens leader Marine Tondelier has urged local officials and parents to wear white and “go and protect our children during demonstrations.”
Amnesty International late Monday said the French authorities should “put an end to the disproportionate police repression seen in recent days during student protests.”
“The images and testimonies widely circulated over the past week raise alarming concerns about the dangerous use of tear gas, batons and policing techniques by the police,” Amnesty’s Anne Savinel-Barras said.
The police have launched 10 internal investigations into allegations of brutality since the protests started, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said late Monday.
Since the start of the movement, 24 schools have been burned or ransacked, according to the education ministry.
More than 5,000 people, 87% of them minors, have been arrested.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office said 85 teaching staff have also been injured.
The government is also pushing legislation to make those responsible for damaging public property pay for repairs themselves, instead of using public funds.

item.title: Yemen fighting kills more than 270 in 24 hours
item.description:
Fighting across Yemen has killed more than 270 government troops and Iran-backed Houthi fighters over the past day, sources on both sides told AFP on Tuesday.
Fighting has intensified in Yemen since the internationally recognized government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia, launched a counter-offensive aimed at recovering territory seized by Houthi fighters last month.
Government sources told AFP on condition of anonymity that 115 troops had died over the past 24 hours, and that dozens of others were wounded in fighting, and by Houthi missile and drone attacks.
The focus of the violence is on southwest Yemen, around the Bab al-Mandab strait that is crucial to global energy flows.
Houthi military sources meanwhile told AFP that they had lost 160 fighters over the past day, mainly in Saudi strikes on areas under their control.

item.title: Qatar says US, Iran still in talks to end war
item.description:
Mediator Qatar on Tuesday said the United States and Iran were still engaged in talks to end the Middle East war, despite an apparent deadlock seven months into the conflict.
The indirect negotiations take account of “the concerns of the various parties,” foreign ministry official Ibrahim Al-Hashmi told a regular press briefing.
“I can confirm that the talks are continuing and the exchange of messages between different parties are continuing via Qatar and its regional partners,” he said.
“As you know, the scale of this conflict and the magnitude of the price that the whole world is paying require us to put our best efforts to end this immediately through a negotiable solution on the negotiation table,” the official added.
Despite a ceasefire in April, a memorandum of understanding in June and talks at the UN General Assembly last month, Washington and Tehran remain at odds over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
On Monday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said talks with the US were “meaningless” and only resulted in renewed attacks, according to state media.

item.title: Iran poised to exploit security vacuum as US leaves Iraq
item.description:
The end of the US military mission in Iraq has created a dangerous security vacuum for the semi-autonomous Kurdish region.
Politicians in Baghdad celebrated the withdrawal, with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi officially declaring October 1 a “Day of Sovereignty and Independence.”
Tehran, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and Iranian-backed Shiite militias also cheered the move.
But in Erbil, the capital of Iraq’s Kurdish region, the mood is markedly more anxious.
Having relied on Washington’s protection for two decades, the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) now faces intertwined crises, including mounting pressure from Baghdad to centralize power and escalating military threats from its neighbors, most notably Iran.
The immediate threat to the Kurdistan region isn’t a full-scale military invasion, but rather a slow, calculated chipping away of its autonomy, said Hesam Dastpish, a Middle East analyst based in Brussels.
He describes Tehran’s overarching strategy toward Erbil as hostile and heavily focused on containment.
The Islamic Republic ultimately wants to strip the KRI of its political clout, reducing it to a purely administrative body, the expert stressed.
“Tehran’s goal is to turn the Kurdistan region into an institution with absolutely no room to maneuver,” Dastpish told DW, pointing to Iran’s repeated strikes in the region, supposedly targeting camps of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups.
Salahuddin Khadiw, a political analyst based in Mahabad in Iran’s Kurdish region, said that neighboring states don’t necessarily want to wipe out Kurdish autonomy completely.
Instead, he underscored, Tehran envisions a “controlled and weak” Kurdistan.
By dealing separately with the rival power centers in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, he argued, Iran has maintained influence across the KRI while seeking to prevent any single Kurdish authority from emerging as a dominant power on its western border.
Despite the external challenges, the Iraqi Kurdish region’s most critical vulnerability comes from within.
The legacy of the 1990s civil war lives on through the deeply entrenched rivalry between the two main ruling factions: the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
Hiwa Mahmoud Osman, an analyst on Iraqi and Kurdish affairs in the Middle East, pointed out that Tehran leans heavily on this internal friction. “Iran has spent decades mastering political influence inside Iraq,” he told DW. “The Kurds’ biggest hurdle is their own fragmentation. Without a united front, foreign powers simply have more room to operate.”
Ardeshir Pashang, a Middle East researcher in Tehran, warned that if Kurdish leaders fail to patch up their political quarrels, this disunity could ultimately lead to the collapse of the Kurdistan region as a political entity.
A particularly thorny issue is the presence of Iranian Kurdish opposition outfits taking refuge in the KRI.
These groups, which have historically clashed with Iranian state forces, are now under immense pressure to disarm and relocate.
Their presence provides Iran with a convenient pretext to launch drone and missile strikes across the border, said Dastpish.
But he doesn’t expect Erbil to offer “total surrender,” as maintaining a balance with these groups is crucial for the KRI’s domestic legitimacy and foreign relations.
Kasra Qaredaghi, a political science researcher based in the US, argues that these groups are now more vulnerable than ever.
If Iran was able to strike their sanctuaries while US forces were still fully deployed — culminating in a 2023 border security pact between Baghdad and Tehran — Erbil’s leverage is now practically non-existent, giving Tehran significantly more power to force concessions, he said.
While US troops may have left, Washington’s leverage in Iraq has not entirely disappeared. It has simply transitioned toward global financial networks. Qaredaghi describes this as a “realignment of power,” where the US, Turkiye, and Saudi Arabia act as natural counterweights to Iran’s growing reach.
Osman echoed this view, highlighting Iraq’s deep financial reliance on the US dollar. This economic tether allows the US Treasury to indirectly influence Baghdad’s internal affairs, right down to ensuring salaries are paid to KRI civil servants.
Khadiw similarly characterizes this strategic pivot as America transitioning from a “military balancer” to a “powerful economic observer.”
But as internal and external pressures mount, the analysts said, Iraq’s Kurdish region may have little choice but to heal its internal divides and present a united front to preserve its autonomy and limit Iran’s strategic gains in the region.

item.title: Son: Wife of jailed ex-Venezuelan leader Maduro has ‘very delicate’ heart issue
item.description:
Venezuelan former first lady Cilia Flores has a “very delicate” heart condition, her son-in-law told AFP on Monday, calling for her release from the US prison where she was jailed alongside Nicolas Maduro.
Flores, 69, was arrested alongside Maduro by US forces during a raid on Caracas on January 3 and taken to the United States to face trial on drug trafficking charges.
She is being held in the same federal prison in Brooklyn, New York, as ousted socialist president Maduro, 63.
Last month, her lawyer requested she be placed under house arrest, saying that she suffers from heart problems for which her prison conditions do not provide adequate care.
The US government opposed the request, arguing she posed “an extreme risk of flight and danger to the public.”
Maduro’s son, Nicolas Maduro Guerra, told AFP that Flores is suffering from a “prolapsed” heart, a condition that, in rare, severe cases, can cause heart failure.
He said that she required surgery and needed to be released from jail in order to properly recuperate afterwards.
Flores’ lawyer Mark Donnelly suggested she be placed under house arrest with 24-hour armed surveillance, an electronic monitoring bracelet and that her passport be confiscated.
Flores, a former president of the National Assembly and attorney general, was seen as a key figure with the repressive Maduro regime.
Both she and Maduro are accused of helping traffic cocaine into the United States, which they deny.
The pair are scheduled to go on trial on June 1, 2027.
Maduro has asked for the charges against him to be dismissed, invoking his immunity as head of state.
In 2015, two of Flores’ nephews were arrested by US officials in Haiti on charges of attempting to traffic cocaine to the United States.
Franqui Francisco Flores de Freitas and Efrain Antonio Campos Flores were each sentenced to 18 years in prison in 2017 but were released in 2022 as part of a prisoner swap deal with the administration of former president Joe Biden.
After Maduro’s ouster, his former deputy Delcy Rodriguez took over as interim president, with the backing of US President Donald Trump.
Rodriguez has appeared ready to comply with Trump’s agenda in Venezuela, including his bid to control vast chunks of the country’s huge oil reserves.

item.title: 180 Directorate of Primary Education officials asked to inspect schools
item.description:
A directive has been issued to deploy 180 officials from the Directorate of Primary Education to different upazilas across the country to conduct on-site inspections, reviews, and observations of primary education activities at the field level.
This directive follows a decision made during the directorate's monthly coordination meeting in August. An office order issued on September 28 published the list of officials alongside their assigned upazilas.
The order instructed the officials to complete their on-site inspections in the designated areas and submit reports by November 5.
According to the office order, senior officials of the directorate, including the director general, additional director general, and directors, are authorised to inspect any upazila in the country.
Additionally, a list has been prepared to deploy officials and staff from various divisions to specific upazilas.
The list covers upazilas across several districts, including Joypurhat, Bogura, Naogaon, Rajshahi, Chapainawabganj, Natore, Sirajganj, Pabna, Kushtia, Meherpur, Chuadanga, and Jhenaidah.
As per the guidelines, officials must obtain prior permission from their respective divisional directors before leaving their duty stations.
Directors will grant permission for officials under their supervision to leave their stations for field-level inspections on a rotational basis.
The order specifies that officials from the Stipend Division must visit the Primary Education Office of their assigned upazila, as well as three government primary schools in the area, following a scheduled tour plan.
These schools are to be selected based on random sampling - one from an urban area and two from rural areas.
The concerned officials are required to stay on-site for two days to conduct the inspection, review, and observation.
Officials from other divisions of the Directorate of Primary Education are required to visit two government primary schools in their assigned upazilas.
They have been instructed to select one urban and one rural school through random sampling and to conduct the inspection, review, and observation while staying on-site for one day.
Upon completion of the inspection, a detailed report must be prepared using the prescribed format and submitted to the Stipend Division of the directorate within five working days.

item.title: From classroom to career: Strengthening professional growth for teachers
item.description:
Teachers are often called the builders of a nation. In Bangladesh, this respect for teachers is deeply rooted in our society. Almost everyone has a teacher they remember someone who encouraged them, guided them or helped shape their future.
But behind this respect is a profession that still faces many challenges. For many teachers, access to quality training remains limited. Career growth is not always clear, and opportunities to improve professional skills often depend on where they work or the resources available to them.
When we discuss education reform, our conversations usually focus on students, textbooks, examinations and curriculum changes. These issues are important, but there is another question we must ask: how are we supporting the people who make education possible?
World Teachers’ Day, observed on October 5, gives us a chance to think about this. This year also marks 60 years since the adoption of the 1966 ILO/UNESCO Recommendation concerning the Status of Teachers, which highlighted the importance of teacher preparation, professional development, rights and working conditions.
The message remains relevant today. A good education system is not built only through policies and infrastructure. It depends largely on the teachers who stand in classrooms every day.
Every successful professional begins with a teacher. Doctors, engineers, entrepreneurs, researchers and public servants all carry lessons they learned from their teachers. The quality of education, therefore, depends greatly on whether teachers themselves receive opportunities to learn and grow.
Teaching is a respected profession, but respect alone is not enough to build a sustainable career. Like professionals in other fields, teachers need proper training, recognition and a clear path for advancement.
Many teachers in Bangladesh still struggle to find that path. A young teacher entering the profession may not always know what opportunities are available after gaining classroom experience. Can they become a senior teacher, academic coordinator, school leader or trainer? What qualifications will help them move forward? In many cases, these questions remain unanswered.
Training opportunities also vary widely. Some teachers have access to workshops, courses and mentoring, while others may have limited opportunities because of location, institutional support or financial challenges.
This affects how young graduates view teaching as a career. Many compares teaching with sectors such as technology, banking, multinational companies and development organizations, where career progression and professional learning systems are often more structured.
If we want talented young people to choose teaching and remain in the profession, we need to create stronger opportunities for growth.
This is not only a challenge for Bangladesh. Countries around the world are facing teacher shortages and difficulties in attracting and retaining skilled educators. According to UNESCO, millions of additional teachers will be needed globally by 2030.
This global demand also shows the changing role of teachers. Today’s teachers need more than subject knowledge. Skills in classroom management, lesson planning, assessment, educational technology and child development are becoming increasingly important.
For Bangladeshi teachers, developing these skills can create opportunities both within the country and internationally.
However, teachers who wish to work abroad need to understand that requirements differ from country to country. There is no single qualification that guarantees a teaching position everywhere. Academic background, teaching experience, professional training, language skills and licensing requirements all play a role.
The Gulf countries, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar, have become destinations for many international teachers. Their international schools often follow British, American, IB and other curricula. Teachers applying for these positions usually need relevant degrees, teaching experience, professional qualifications and good communication skills.
Europe offers opportunities as well, but the process can be more complicated. In many countries, teaching is a regulated profession. Foreign qualifications may need assessment, additional certification or local language skills.
England also has specific requirements for overseas-trained teachers. While some teachers may work in certain situations without immediately obtaining Qualified Teacher Status (QTS), it remains an important qualification for many long-term teaching careers.
Therefore, teachers should research carefully before choosing professional qualifications or planning an international career.
For English-language teachers, qualifications such as Cambridge’s Teaching Knowledge Test (TKT) can support professional learning by improving understanding of teaching methods, lesson planning and classroom practices. However, it should be seen as a professional development qualification, not a universal teaching license.
Teachers working with young children can also benefit from Early Childhood Development (ECD) training. Understanding child behavior, learning through play, classroom safety and child development is essential for effective early-years education.
Learning should not stop when a teacher enters the classroom. In many ways, teaching itself is a lifelong learning profession.
Bangladesh needs more accessible ways for teachers to continue developing their skills. Training should not be something available only to a few; it should become a regular part of every teacher’s professional journey.
Workshops, mentoring programmes, online courses, teacher networks and recognized certifications can help create more learning opportunities.
Private initiatives can also play a role. Platforms such as Teachers Time provide training opportunities in areas including English-language teaching, Early Childhood Development, classroom management, child development and project-based learning.
Such platforms cannot replace universities or formal teacher-training institutions, but they can support teachers who may not otherwise have easy access to professional learning.
Building a stronger teacher-development system requires cooperation among schools, universities, government agencies, development organisations and education technology companies.
Different teachers need different kinds of support. A mathematics teacher may want to improve assessment techniques. An English teacher may seek international teaching qualifications. An early-years educator may need deeper knowledge of child psychology. A school leader may require training in management and leadership.
Professional development should become a natural part of teaching, not something teachers have to discover on their own.
On World Teachers’ Day, we often remember the teachers who influenced our lives. That appreciation matters, but teachers need more than appreciation.
They need opportunities to grow.
A young teacher starting a career in Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi, Khulna or a rural school should be able to see a future ahead — becoming a senior teacher, curriculum specialist, school leader, teacher trainer or international educator.
Sixty years after the ILO/UNESCO recommendation, Bangladesh has an opportunity to rethink how teachers are supported. The question is not only whether we respect teachers, but whether we provide them with the tools, training and opportunities they need to build meaningful careers.
If we want better education outcomes, investing in teachers must be at the heart of that effort.
Tahmina Rahman is an author, teacher trainer of Teachers Time. She can be reached at tahmina.sathi90@gmail.com

item.title: India opposition leaders briefly detained in election protest
item.description:
India’s opposition leader Rahul Gandhi was briefly detained by police on Tuesday during a march protesting against the Election Commission, demanding its chief resign and alleging wrongdoing during a revision of voter rolls.
An AFP reporter saw Gandhi, a leader of the Congress Party, standing on a police barricade and waving an Indian flag. Officers detained him briefly, along with other lawmakers, and then released them soon after.
Opposition parties began their march from parliament towards to the Election Commission of India (ECI), but were stopped by heavy police deployments. Some politicians sat down on the street to wait.
Protests began on Friday, demanding that commission chief Gyanesh Kumar step down.
Opposition politicians have accused the commission of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, saying the revision process is aimed at ensuring the accuracy and integrity of electoral rolls.
Kumar has not commented publicly.
“Gyanesh, it’s done, bro,” placards read, as well as signs alleging electoral manipulation.
Opposition leaders pressed their demands for greater transparency in the revision of voter lists, alleging that changes to the rolls could disenfranchise eligible voters.
The protest was part of a wider campaign against the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
The issue of voter deletion was reignited by a report in September by The Indian Express newspaper, which said two of the ECI’s three members had formally objected at least 14 times to key decisions linked to the voter roll revision.
The news report claimed the names of 130 million citizens had been deleted since the exercise began in 2025.
